clue.text: Flippant curate terminally throttled by dissident

indicators.note: something throttled is gripped around the neck, so the dissident word closes round the curate's letter

parts.note: factious describes a dissenting, quarrelsome faction

indicators.note: terminally points to the very end of the word curate

explanation.surface: A rebellious type strangles a curate who was being too light-hearted.
explanation.definitionFit: A facetious remark is jokey when seriousness is wanted, which is what flippant means.

clue.text: Serving to supplement fine beer contaminated with sulphur

parts.note: F is the pencil-grade abbreviation for fine

indicators.note: beer contaminated with something has it mixed in, so the element goes inside

parts.note: ale is a type of beer
S is the chemical symbol for sulphur

explanation.surface: A good pint has been tainted by a sulphurous taint.
explanation.walkthrough: The sense is the technical one, as in false ribs or a false keel added to a structure.
explanation.definitionFit: In building and anatomy, a false part is an additional or substitute one supplementing the main structure.

clue.text: Mounted soldier, having excelled all round, had little sleep

indicators.note: all round means surrounding, so the outdoing word wraps the insect

parts.note: capped means outdid or surpassed

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means raised up, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a soldier is a type of ant

explanation.surface: A cavalryman who has outperformed everyone takes a quick nap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mounted' suggests a horse, but in this down light it means ANT is written upwards, giving TNA.
explanation.definitionFit: To catnap is to take a short, light doze, so had a little sleep.

clue.text: Sinner's very French monarch attending ball

parts.note: très is French for very
a pass is a ball played to a teammate
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the late Queen's cipher

explanation.surface: A wicked French king seen at a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes the Lord's Prayer: 'forgive those who trespass against us'.
explanation.definitionFit: In biblical language to trespass is to sin, so a trespasser is a sinner.

clue.text: Keep watch

definitions.meaning: to keep a rule or a festival, honour it
to watch is to look closely at

explanation.definitionFit: One verb covers both honouring a custom or law and looking carefully at something.

clue.text: Thomas perhaps about to feed pussy?

indicators.note: feeding puts something into the mouth, so the letter is put inside

parts.note: pussy here means full of pus, infected
C stands for circa, Latin for about

explanation.surface: Someone named Thomas is about to give the cat its dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pussy' looks like a cat but means pus-filled. Doubting Thomas, the apostle who would not believe without proof, is the archetype.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubting Thomas, the apostle who wanted proof of the Resurrection, is the classic example of a doubter.

clue.text: Once defiant island area with spirit

parts.note: malt is short for malt whisky, a spirit

explanation.surface: An island known for resistance, with plenty of land and plenty of courage.
explanation.walkthrough: MALTA was awarded the George Cross in 1942 for withstanding the Axis siege, hence 'once defiant'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean island held out under prolonged wartime bombardment, earning a collective George Cross.

clue.text: Husband or wife making tea?

definitions.meaning: the South American herbal infusion made from yerba leaves

explanation.surface: A spouse puts the kettle on.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a partner in marriage and, accented, a South American herbal infusion.

clue.text: In while selling up — one has to leave

indicators.note: something that has to leave is taken away from the word
in a down clue, up means the word is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: retail means selling to the public
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: During a sales drive, one staff member is forced out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RETAIL into LIATER, and 'has to leave' removes I.
explanation.definitionFit: Later means after some time has passed, as in 'see you in a while'.

clue.text: Cool Paris knocked around in Athenian citadel

indicators.note: letters knocked around are jumbled into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A trendy Parisian is jostled while touring a Greek landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: The Acropolis is the fortified hilltop in Athens crowned by the Parthenon.

clue.text: Stream of consciousness? On the contrary!

definitions.text: Stream of consciousness? On the contrary!

parts.words: Stream of consciousness? On the contrary!
parts.note: the clue wants a stream that brings the opposite of consciousness: the river of the classical underworld whose water made the dead forget

explanation.walkthrough: 'Stream of consciousness' is a literary technique; reversing it gives a river of oblivion, the one in Hades whose waters wiped the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth this underworld river induced forgetfulness, the opposite of awareness.

clue.text: Boxing ace, Prescott walloped onlooker

indicators.note: boxing here means enclosing, as in a box, so the scrambled name surrounds the card letter
walloped suggests the name has been knocked about into a new order

parts.note: A is the usual abbreviation for an ace in cards

explanation.surface: John Prescott, the former UK Deputy Prime Minister who famously punched a protester, gets hit by a boxing champion while someone watches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing' places A inside SPECTTOR, the anagram of PRESCOTT signalled by 'walloped'.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator watches an event without taking part, exactly an onlooker.

clue.text: Annoy divorcee worried about stewed pears

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse

indicators.note: stewed fruit is cooked down into a mess, so the letters of pears are jumbled

parts.note: ate, as in what's eating you, means worried or troubled

explanation.surface: A former spouse frets over a dessert of poached pears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is loose: it must mean 'next to', since the worried word follows the fruit rather than surrounding it. Worried as in 'what's eating him?'.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate someone is to irritate them intensely, a strong synonym for annoy.

clue.text: Support for progressives' leader

parts.note: pro means in favour of, so for

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of progressives'

explanation.surface: Someone declares backing for the head of the progressive movement.
explanation.definitionFit: A prop is a physical or figurative support that holds something up.

clue.text: Northern town's battling heavyweight?

parts.note: warring means fighting
a ton is a very heavy weight

explanation.surface: A northern town known for a fighting champion boxer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heavyweight' suggests a boxer; it is the unit of mass. Warrington is a town in Cheshire, in north-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: Warrington is a town in Cheshire, between Liverpool and Manchester in north-west England.

clue.text: Setter is past prime coming to standstill

parts.note: the setter refers to themself, so the setter is becomes I'm
passé means outdated, past one's best

explanation.surface: The crossword compiler admits to fading powers, and their work grinding to a halt.
explanation.walkthrough: The setter speaking of themself gives I'M, a standard crossword convention.
explanation.definitionFit: An impasse is a deadlock where no progress is possible, a standstill.

clue.text: Romantics plan to hear from Poets Society

parts.note: an idea is a plan or scheme
list is an archaic verb meaning to listen or hear

explanation.surface: Members of a poetry society propose listening to Romantic verse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from Poets' only links the surface; 'list', archaic for listen, as in Hamlet's 'List, list, O list!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idealists pursue perfect visions over practical reality, the same impractical cast as romantics.

clue.text: Where choir sings hymn's opening line

parts.note: a chance is an opportunity, an opening

explanation.surface: The first line of a hymn, as sung by a church choir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening' looks like 'first' attached to hymn's, but means an opportunity.
explanation.definitionFit: The chancel is the part of a church near the altar containing the choir stalls.

clue.text: With gin and ale getting sloshed is nice

parts.note: con is Italian and Spanish for with

indicators.note: getting sloshed means getting drunk, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink of gin with beer makes everything pleasant.
explanation.definitionFit: Congenial company is pleasant and agreeable, a synonym for nice.

clue.text: Enduring without purpose?

parts.note: an end is an aim or purpose
less means without, as in a suffix like hopeless

explanation.surface: Putting up with something while having no aim in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Something endless goes on and on, lasting indefinitely, so enduring.

clue.text: Implements third-rate accommodation in steamship

indicators.note: in places the shabby dwelling inside the ship's abbreviation

parts.note: SS is the prefix for a steamship
a hovel is squalid housing

explanation.surface: Someone puts into effect a scheme of poor cabins aboard a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Implements' reads as a verb but is the plural noun: tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Shovels are digging tools, so examples of implements.

clue.text: Serving men in battle ultimately dividing spoils

indicators.note: something dividing a word splits it apart by sitting in the middle of it

parts.note: mars means spoils or ruins

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the closing letter of battle

explanation.surface: Soldiers sharing out the plunder once the fighting is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Marines are soldiers serving with the navy, men in military service.

clue.text: Beastly fighter Mike runs round at a party

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the first two letters enclose the party phrase

parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A man called Mike hurries about at a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A matador is the bullfighter who kills the bull, so one who fights a beast.

clue.text: Sky will do play-off cricket finals

indicators.note: finals are the last letters of the four words that follow

explanation.surface: Sky Sports promises to televise the deciding cricket matches.
explanation.walkthrough: Sky is the satellite broadcaster in the surface, but a verb here: to hit high in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: To sky a ball, as in cricket, is to hit it high, the same as to loft it.

clue.text: Certain measures taken about student in prison

indicators.note: taken about means placed around, so the measures surround the learner

parts.note: feet are specific units of length
L stands for learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: Steps are taken concerning a student who is locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: The Fleet was a notorious London prison, used largely for debtors until 1842.
explanation.definitionFit: The Fleet Prison was a historic London jail, so the name stands for a prison.

clue.text: Massive area hosts grand party

indicators.note: a host contains its guests, so the large landmass holds the letter

parts.note: a continent is a huge expanse of land
G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A huge venue puts on a big celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' reads as a celebration but means a group of people.
explanation.definitionFit: A contingent is a group sent or attending together, a party in that sense.

clue.text: Cheap booze that's no good upset teacher

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means turned upside down, so read from bottom to top
no good means the good letter is dropped

parts.note: rotgut is cheap, poor-quality liquor

explanation.surface: A teacher is ill after drinking bad liquor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' removes G from ROTGUT, leaving ROTUT, which 'upset' turns over.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or university instructor.

clue.text: Bankers withdrawing from hunting expedition miles away

indicators.note: bankers are the letters on either side of a word, like a river's banks, and here they leave it

parts.note: a safari is a hunting trip, traditionally in Africa

explanation.surface: Financiers pull out of a hunting trip far from home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bankers' suggests financiers; it means the two edge letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Afar means at a great distance, so a long way off.

clue.text: Fife's held after riot in northern city

indicators.note: after a riot everything is thrown into disorder, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Fife, a Scottish region, has stayed in control after unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheffield is a large city in South Yorkshire in the north of England.

clue.text: Dance an unexpected event

definitions.meaning: a dance craze of the early 1960s
a surprise development in a story or situation

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both the 1960s rock-and-roll dance and a sudden plot turn.

clue.text: It's time to meet your god

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, abbreviated SA
yr is a written abbreviation of your

explanation.surface: An announcement that the moment has come for you to meet your maker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: A satyr is a woodland deity of Greek myth, part man and part goat, a minor divinity.

clue.text: Alien grabbing Lambert's face is killer

indicators.note: something grabbing a letter holds it in its grip, inside

parts.note: a stranger is someone foreign or unfamiliar

indicators.note: the face of a word is its front, the first letter of Lambert's

explanation.surface: An alien creature seizes a person called Lambert by the face, horror-film style.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface recalls Lambert, the crew member killed in the film Alien.
explanation.definitionFit: A strangler kills by choking, so is a killer of a particular kind.
